scenes.voiceover: There's a star in tonight's sky that could explode at any moment.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: red supergiant star seething in darkness

scenes.voiceover: Betelgeuse. The red shoulder of Orion. Seven hundred times bigger than our sun.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: orion constellation with betelgeuse glowing red

scenes.voiceover: And it is dying. In 2019 it suddenly dimmed so hard, astronomers thought this was it.
When it finally goes, it will outshine the full moon. Visible in daylight, for months.
scenes.mainText: it will OUTSHINE THE MOON for months
scenes.visualConcept: night sky gaining a second light source
scenes.backgroundPrompt: supernova visible in a daytime sky over a city

scenes.voiceover: Here's the strangest part. Its light takes six hundred years to reach us. It may have already exploded.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: light traveling across centuries of space

scenes.voiceover: The explosion could be racing toward us right now. And we won't know until the night it arrives.
scenes.mainText: we won't know until the night it ARRIVES
scenes.backgroundPrompt: wave of supernova light approaching earth

scenes.voiceover: Look up at Orion tonight. You might catch history. Follow mindwired for more.
